description: Structural wire contract; native validation also checks indices, lengths and cross-field invariants.

mode.description: auto, panels, or anything else to smooth every arc (source clean_chart)

enhanced.description: enhanced_v1 proposal policy: objective weights (Section 11.2), per-chart search bounds (Section 21) and strict-validity tolerances; legacy_010 and native_baseline ignore it

boundary_refinement.description: enhanced_v1: every new or changed seam chain of a region, ring, cavity or shell proposal goes through the baseline's chain refinement (corridors, turn, flow, drift, convexity and the crease-discounted exposure) inside the proposal's faces before the transaction evaluates it (requires refine_paths)

cavities.description: enhanced_v1 confidence-gated cavity proposals (T36): same-component cone rays on the geometry BVH (samples, rays, cone, reach as a fraction of the component diagonal), refinement levels, detector filters and bounds

constraint_repair.description: enhanced_v1 constraint repair of painted hard constraints (T29, Section 21 step 1; an ablation switch): off, a candidate zero violating required or forbidden edges gets no repair proposal and such a run is refused (constraint_conflict); the constraints themselves are never relaxed

endpoint_slide.description: enhanced_v1 sliding seam endpoints on tube-like patches (T30/T31): optional maximum slide distance along a rim (0 disables it), whole-patch search vertex budget and route cost weights

significance.description: seam_objective.v2 significance rule (enhanced_v1): where the exposure-sampling margin U applies, a change decided by J is adopted only when it lowers J by more than max(U, practical_floor * |J of the incumbent|); a change that only removes seam edges has no floor, and budget, compliance and strict-defect decisions never see it

version.description: the ordering over J: seam_objective.v1 compares J within the tie band only (T40); seam_objective.v2 also treats a J difference within the sampling uncertainty of the raw exposure term as a tie that keeps the incumbent

preferences.description: enhanced_v1 painted preferences (T29): routing heuristic weights and the host attribute names read for required/forbidden edges and allow/avoid points (documented names or explicit aliases; empty disables one)

regions.description: enhanced_v1 preference-aware region proposals (T34): dual crossing weight centroid_distance * (1 + w_normal*normal_change + w_preference*strength^2), Lloyd steps and targets per pass

keep_feature_seams.description: GB (visual review V3): the incumbent's seams on hard feature edges (|dihedral| at least the baseline seam cost's feature angle; never a painted forbidden edge) bound the region growth like required and locked cuts and stay cut wherever the regrown regions meet across them

relief.description: enhanced_v1 sector-aware hotspot relief (T32; settings: native record hotspot_relief.v1)

rings.description: enhanced_v1 constriction/crease ring proposals (T35): distance-level sections from a patch opening, the confidence gate and the candidate bounds per chart and pass

scale.description: enhanced_v1 physical-distance policy (T39): physical (geodesic corridors, area floors and smoothing in object-space units frozen at the operation start; explicit reference_length, reference_area and corridor_radius for cross-tessellation work) or hops (the legacy hop-ring corridors, face-count floors and step counts, for comparisons with native_baseline)

search.description: enhanced_v1 bounded alternative search (T40, Section 21): each feature's share of the per-chart candidate and solve bounds, and whether a candidate whose exact objective proves it cannot win is refused before its solve

shells.description: enhanced_v1 thin-shell front/back rim proposals (T37): nominating thickness ratio, opposite-side correspondence and confidence gates, label smoothing and speckle repair, alternatives per component (baseline included)

spur_removal.description: enhanced_v1 validated unnecessary-spur removal (T33; the legacy spur cleanup is unchanged)

strict_repair.description: enhanced_v1 validated strict-overlap repair (Section 11.3 policy; native record strict_overlap_repair.v1): candidate zero's charts that fail only the strict overlap check are re-mapped or minimally split through the transaction; a defect left unrepaired is reported and keeps native_baseline's decision

symmetry.description: enhanced_v1 operational symmetry (T38): asymmetric (view-optimal, unpaired moves), strict (every move paired with its mirror image as one transaction on an exact combinatorial correspondence) or approximate (metric-only diagnostics); the conflict policy, an explicit or detected plane, the counterpart and strict geometry tolerances (fractions of the bounding-box diagonal) and the symmetrization alternatives per pass

host.description: Blender settings carried with the options for the host; the engine and the command line do not read them

max_defect.description: null means unbounded legacy angle-defect proxy; no nonfinite number is accepted

priority.description: compact, small_first, or anything else for longest-arc order (source merge_patches)

seeding.description: auto, motorcycle or voronoi; any other value is refused when seams are generated (source generate_seams)

solver.description: lscm, harmonic, or anything else for ARAP (source flatten_chart)

corridor_max_rings.description: any integer under legacy_010; at least 1 under other policies (FIX-02)

corridor_rings.description: any integer under legacy_010 (the source searches from it); at least 1 under other policies (FIX-02)

variants.description: legacy_010 only: the fixed weight variants the source searches; other policies derive them from w_turn, w_flow and w_drift (FIX-01)

backend.description: recorded, not a selector: the pipeline's sparse solves use the SciPy-compatible numerical policy

iterations.description: iterations a host session asks the host's unwrap for; the core backend uses 10 (source CoreBackend)

method.description: recorded, not a selector: the core backend always runs ARAP (source CoreBackend) and a host session the host's unwrap
